title: WiSI: Wireless-in-the-Loop Self-Improvement
summary: WiSI evaluates language-model-driven program improvement under wireless execution feedback. In the reported tasks, agents improved under ideal links achieved 40.0% success under congestion, compared with 77.2% for agents improved under realistic wireless conditions. The result is limited to the tested setup.
ai_technology: Large language model-driven program improvement evaluated in a wireless-in-the-loop framework
organization: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, The University of Hong Kong

evidence.tested: A controlled comparison found 40.0% task success under congestion for agents improved under ideal links, versus 77.2% for agents improved with realistic wireless conditions. The authors report retained communication-efficient program structures.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to the studied tasks, agent and wireless simulation; real-world deployment generalization is not established.
evidence.ai_role: WiSI uses an LLM to propose program changes; execution feedback is generated under modeled wireless conditions and informs candidate selection.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
